File:Scouting Report 1 player peaked.png|My personal best time (achieved for the {{badge|Speed Climber}}) which I'm unlikely to try and improve. == Tutorial == Because I use Linux, I use a convoluted method for taking screenshots that most people shouldn't use. This tutorial is for myself, but also other Linux users. If you're a Windows user, [[Meta:Image guide|here are the instructions for you]]. In order to get the highest possible quality screenshots of the game, in my Steam settings I have In Game > Save an external copy of my screenshots turned on. Then, from the pictures I take in-game, I choose the best ones to crop and remove the crosshair from before uploading them. I crop and remove the crosshair from screenshots using [[wikipedia:GIMP|GIMP]]. Depending on where the crosshair is placed, I may be able to get away with using the '''Paintbrush''', but if not, I have to hope that I can use the '''Clone Tool''' to patch it out and still keep the picture looking real. I use the following brush settings: * Brush: 2. Hardness 050 * Size: 5.00 * Aspect Ratio: 0.00 * Angle: 0.00 * Spacing: 10.00 * Hardness: 0.00 * Force: 50.00 I wish there was a way to disable the [[heads up display]] without installing any mods, it would make taking these screenshots a lot easier. {{clear}} = Ideas = {{Ambox | color = #ff4d00 | icon = Guidebook Locations.png | title = Fictional Content | message = The material presented here is purely fictional and does not exist in {{peak_game}}, nor may it be added in the future. | tiny = | date = | class = }} == Realism == [[File:Guidebook HowTo.png|right|240px]] '''Realism''' is an optional modifier for all [[Ascents]] that is toggled via a checkbox which appears when using the [[Airport#Kiosks|Gate Kiosk]]. When Realism is turned on, the [[heads up display]] is completely disabled apart from the game version number, ascent information, {{item|Backpack}} menu and pause menu, hiding [[Scout|player names]], the [[stamina bar]] and player [[inventories]]. Players must rely entirely on the sound cues and vignettes shown by the game to determine how much stamina they have and are using. In particular: * The sound effect when beginning to use {{bonus}} still plays. Climbing speed is used to determine the point at which a [[Scout]] is about to run out of stamina. * {{hunger}} produces subtle stomach growling, which grows louder and more frequent the hungrier a Scout is. * {{injury}} produces the sound of a heartbeat, which grows more aggressive the more hurt a Scout is, but its speed is dependent on external factors. * {{poison}} is displayed as a purple vignette. * {{cold}} is displayed as a light blue vignette. * {{heat}} is displayed as an orange vignette. * {{thorns}} appear along the side of the screen while on a Scout. * {{drowsy}} is displayed as an eyelid overlay, which blinks and begins to close as a Scout grows tired. * {{curse}} is displayed as [[wikipedia:Macular degeneration|macular degeneration]] overlays, which appear and disappear slowly and infrequently, causing the screen to warp. With high levels of Curse, more of these overlays appear. [[Island]] summits completed with Realism enabled are listed as a separate item in the [[Accolades]] menu, underneath total summits. Alive players that are rescued from the [[Peak]] with Realism enabled gain the '''Crescendo Badge'''. Doing so on Ascent 7 grants the '''Survivor Badge'''. == The Chained == {{Infobox | Name = The Chained | image = Scout physics bug.png | Type = [[NPC]] ([[:Category:Enemies|Hostile]]) }} ''(Editor's note: I am very surprised by how close this idea of mine came to what was eventually implemented in [[Roots]], that being [[Zombies]].)'' '''The Chained''' is a hostile [[NPC]] in {{peak_game}}. It can be encountered in any region 2 or 3 [[biome]] (e.g. [[Tropics]], [[Alpine]], [[Mesa]]) and appears in both singleplayer and multiplayer. The Chained puts pressure on a [[Scout]] troop by encouraging its members to separate. It has two behavioural states: '''passive''' and '''active'''. === Gameplay === ==== Spawning ==== At the beginning of a game, there is a 10% chance The Chained will be set to spawn, either in region 2 or 3 (both equally likely). From then, if on the biome The Chained should spawn in, half or more of the Scout troop have reached the vertical climb portion of the biome, and no environmental hazard (e.g. [[rain]], [[blizzard]], [[Mesa#Sun|hot sun]]) is active, it will spawn in the '''passive''' state. ==== Passive state ==== The Chained spawns out in the open in a position that is not being observed by any player, and will immediately begin to walk and climb (with infinite stamina) towards the closest Scout on the vertical climb. While in its passive state, The Chained takes on the appearance of a random Scout not yet on the vertical climb (or the lone Scout in single-player), with the exception of slightly washed-out skin colour, pupil-less eyes, a {{item|Chain Launcher}} in its crooked, locked-in-place hands, and chains that extend from its hands down its back. It keeps its head low and faces towards Scouts to hide these telltale signs of its presence. In multiplayer, if all players stop observing it before it enters its active state, it will despawn. ==== Active state ==== The Chained will enter its '''active''' state if: * It gets too close to a Scout. * In multiplayer, it is observed for 5 seconds total (before despawning). * In single-player, it has been 5 seconds after it was first observed. In the active state, The Chained raises its head, begins to let out a haunting screech and gains the ability to climb along any surface regardless of orientation. While a player is observing it or is very close to it, they will steadily be inflicted with {{curse}}. The amount of Curse applied by The Chained depletes only when not observing it nor close to it. If The Chained is unable to quickly reach its targets due to vertical distance, it will fire its Chain Launcher (once only) in the direction of one of its targets, having a high chance of hitting and pinning them temporarily if they are in its line of sight, and will climb up the chain before resuming its standard active behaviour. Once all players are far enough from The Chained so as to not hear its screeching anymore, it will despawn.

'''Badges''', also known as '''Accolades''' and '''Achievements''', are granted to players of {{Peak game}} upon completing certain actions. Once obtained, they are displayed on the [[Scout]]'s equipped [[sash]]. Every badge has an associated reward [[cosmetic]] item. A full list of badges can be viewed in-game on the Accolades screen accessible via the pause menu. Hovering over a badge shows its name and description. Badges which are not yet unlocked are greyed out, with their names replaced with question marks. The player's current [[sash]] and successful expeditions count are also shown. [[Equipment#Mystical Items|Mythical Items]] that could pratically reduce {{Hunger}} (e.g. {{Item|Cure-All}}) are ''not'' disscussed here. == Usage == Food items can be used by holding {{Key|mouse|left}}'''left click''' while holding in hand. [eating time placeholder, lack of data]. Most foods are single-use, except {{Item|Scout Cookies}}, which have 4 uses in total. The main use of foods is to restore stamina by reducing {{Hunger}}. Most foods reduce certain amount of {{Hunger}}, but some foods, like {{Item|Sports Drink}}, do not. All cooked food and some uncooked food also add {{Bonus}} to [[Stamina bar]]. Some foods, like {{Item|Scorchberry}} and {{Item|Medicinal Root}}, inflict or remove additional [[Stamina bar#Status effects|status effects]]. {{Poison}}, {{Spores}}, {{Heat}}, {{Thorns}} and {{Drowsy}} may be obtained from foods. When a food item Some foods have special effects when used. The effects of all foods are listed below. == Cooking == [[Cooking]] food is a way to improve the food's quality. Cooked food always reduce more {{Hunger}} and add more {{Bonus}} than its uncooked version (if exists). Cooking can also remove hazardous effects, like {{Poison}} or {{Spores}}, from certain foods that have them. So in terms of nutritious values, it's always a good idea to cook the food before eating if available. However, [[Cooking#Cooking stages|overcooking]] could make foods' quality worse by lowering {{Hunger}} values and adding {{Poison}} to them. Certain food like {{Item|Energy Drink}} reacts differently after cooking, which may backfire in some circumstances. == Sources == Foods can be obtained in two major ways in game: naturally generated in the world or found inside luggages. === Naturally generated === - generation - special not directly consumable food items - physcal/interactions A major source of foods is foraging for foods generated on the [[Island]]. Different types of foods can be found in different [[Biomes]]. Most naturally generated foods, especially [[Berries]], are gerenated in specific locations. For example, [[Crispberry|Crispberries]] only appear in the bushes. The foods' spawn locations are determined by the seed [not confirmed], but the numbers of items (can be 0) are not consistent in different runs.
